title: Cone model comparison after the ordinary-base target change
statement: Use simplicial sets, ordinary nerves, coherent realization, ordered cone pushouts and enriched diagrams as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], [lem-coef-unmarked-straightening-quillen], [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation], [lem-coef-unmarked-straightening-target-change], [lem-coef-enriched-diagram-rectification], [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus] and [lem-coef-simplicial-presheaf-projective-model]. Let $C$ be a small ordinary category, $B=N(C)$, $S=B^{\mathrm{op}}$, let $p:X\to B$ be any simplicial map, and let $D:C\to\mathsf{Kan}_{\mathcal U}$ be a strict Kan-valued diagram, i.e. an ordinary functor to the category of $\mathcal U$-small Kan complexes. Write $D^{\mathrm{op}}:C\to\mathsf{sSet}$ for the valuewise opposite $c\mapsto D(c)^{\mathrm{op}}$, with the same indexing category $C$. Put $A=\mathfrak C[S]^{\mathrm{op}}\cong\mathfrak C[B]$, let $\epsilon:\mathfrak C[S]\to C^{\mathrm{op}}$ be the counit of $\mathfrak C\dashv N_{\mathrm{hc}}$ (using $N_{\mathrm{hc}}(C^{\mathrm{op}})=N(C^{\mathrm{op}})=S$) and $u=\epsilon^{\mathrm{op}}:A\to C$, and let $P=T_S(X^{\mathrm{op}})$ be the ordered-cone diagram of [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation]. Then $u$ is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence, $P$ is projectively cofibrant, and the target-change isomorphism identifies $u_!P$ naturally with the cone diagram $H_C(X)=L_\epsilon(X^{\mathrm{op}}):C\to\mathsf{sSet}$ of [lem-coef-unmarked-straightening-target-change], $c\mapsto(\mathfrak C[X^{\mathrm{op}}\star\Delta^0]\amalg_{\mathfrak C[X^{\mathrm{op}}]}C^{\mathrm{op}})(c,v)$, with the pushout formed along $\epsilon\,\mathfrak C[p^{\mathrm{op}}]$. If $w:u_!P\to D^{\mathrm{op}}$ is an objectwise weak homotopy equivalence, its enriched Kan-extension adjoint $P\to u^*D^{\mathrm{op}}$ is an objectwise weak equivalence; the cone Quillen-equivalence criterion then gives a contravariant weak equivalence $X^{\mathrm{op}}\to U_S(u^*D^{\mathrm{op}})$ and, after taking opposites, a covariant weak equivalence $X\to U_B^{\mathrm{cov}}(u^*D^{\mathrm{op}})$. All these maps are natural in $X$ and in maps of strict Kan diagrams.

source.place: Remark 3.2.5.10 and Lemma 3.2.5.17(1), Proposition 3.2.5.18(1), together with the enriched projective Quillen criterion and the ordinary covariant presentation

proof.text: Regard $C^{\mathrm{op}}$ as a simplicial category with discrete mapping sets. These sets are Kan: in every positive-dimensional horn all specified vertices have the same value, and the constant simplex is a filler (the empty set has no horn maps). The discrete-category clause of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison] identifies $N_{\mathrm{hc}}(C^{\mathrm{op}})$ with $N(C^{\mathrm{op}})=S$. Hence the counit clause of [lem-coef-enriched-diagram-rectification], applied to $C^{\mathrm{op}}$, says that $\epsilon:\mathfrak C[S]\to C^{\mathrm{op}}$ is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence. Its opposite is the specified $u:A\to C$. For $a,b$, the map on mapping sets for $u$ is exactly that for $\epsilon$ at $(b,a)$, and $\pi_0(u)=\pi_0(\epsilon)^{\mathrm{op}}$. Taking the opposite of an equivalence and its inverse preserves the inverse identities. The cited counit clause gives weak homotopy equivalences on mapping sets and essential surjectivity on $\pi_0$; the former give bijections on components, so $\pi_0(\epsilon)$ is also fully faithful, hence an equivalence. Thus $u$ is Dwyer--Kan in the sense of [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus]. The ordered-reversal isomorphism of [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation] identifies $A=\mathfrak C[S]^{\mathrm{op}}$ with $\mathfrak C[B]$.

source.place: Theorem 2.2.0.1, printed p.72; proof of Corollary 2.2.5.6, p.93; opposite of the counit.

proof.text: In the contravariant slice model structure over $S$, every object is cofibrant by [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation]: the initial map $\varnothing\to X^{\mathrm{op}}$ is a monomorphism. The same node gives the left Quillen functor $T_S$ into $A$-diagrams. Apply its preservation of cofibrations to that initial map. Since a left adjoint preserves the initial object, its image is the initial map into $P=T_S(X^{\mathrm{op}})$, which is therefore projectively cofibrant. This uses no fibration hypothesis on $X\to B$.

source.place: Remark 2.1.4.12 and Theorem 2.2.1.2, printed pp.71 and 74.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-unmarked-straightening-target-change] with its target categories $D=A$, $D'=C$, its $\phi=\mathrm{id}_{\mathfrak C[S]}:\mathfrak C[S]\to A^{\mathrm{op}}$, and its $\pi=u$. Its composite $\pi^{\mathrm{op}}\phi$ is $\epsilon$. The identity-target ordered-cone functor is $T_S$, by its displayed pushout in [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation]. The changed-target cone functor is $L_\epsilon$, so the target-change isomorphism is $\beta_X:u_!P\xrightarrow{\cong}L_\epsilon(X^{\mathrm{op}})=H_C(X)$. Explicitly, the last value at $c$ is $(\mathfrak C[X^{\mathrm{op}}\star\Delta^0]\amalg_{\mathfrak C[X^{\mathrm{op}}]}C^{\mathrm{op}})(c,v)$, with action by precomposition. This is exactly the cone construction of [lem-coef-unmarked-straightening-quillen]. The attaching map is $\epsilon\mathfrak C[p^{\mathrm{op}}]$, where $p:X\to B$. The isomorphism is natural in $X$ by the cited target-change statement; no local Kan condition on $\mathfrak C[S]$ is needed.

source.place: Section 2.2.1, printed p.73, and Proposition 2.2.1.1(2), p.74; ordinary-base specialization of Remark 3.2.5.10.

proof.text: Here $D^{\mathrm{op}}$ means the strict diagram $c\mapsto D(c)^{\mathrm{op}}$, applying the simplicial opposite to every value and every map, with indexing category still $C$. Opposite preserves Kan complexes by [lem-coef-infinity-opposite-subdivision-kan-zigzag]. Thus $D^{\mathrm{op}}$ is objectwise Kan. Apply [lem-coef-simplicial-presheaf-projective-model] to the ordinary category $C^{\mathrm{op}}$: its presheaves are precisely these covariant $C$-diagrams, and its fibrant-object clause makes $D^{\mathrm{op}}$ projectively fibrant. Restriction gives $(u^*D^{\mathrm{op}})(a)=D(u(a))^{\mathrm{op}}$, again Kan; the projective fibrancy clause of [lem-coef-unmarked-straightening-quillen] makes this a fibrant $A$-diagram. The Kan-model category of simplicial sets is combinatorial and simplicial by the first clause of the presheaf-model node.

source.place: Simplicial opposite convention; Example A.3.2.18 and Proposition A.3.3.2, with the objectwise projective fibrancy convention.

proof.text: Use [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus] with the combinatorial simplicial Kan-model category of simplicial sets, $I=A$, $J=C$ and $v=u$. Smallness of $A$ follows from the coherent-realization construction on the small simplicial set $S$, and $C$ is small by hypothesis. Step 1 verifies the Dwyer--Kan hypothesis. Its enriched Kan-extension/restriction adjunction $u_!\dashv u^*$ is therefore a Quillen equivalence. Step 2 supplies the cofibrant source $P$, and step 4 the fibrant target $D^{\mathrm{op}}$. The given $w:u_!P\to D^{\mathrm{op}}$ is a weak equivalence in the projective model structure, since these are objectwise weak homotopy equivalences. The exact cofibrant-source/fibrant-target criterion in the cited node now gives a projective weak equivalence $f:P\to u^*D^{\mathrm{op}}$, the adjoint of $w$. In unit notation it is $f=u^*w\circ\eta^u_P$. Consequently $f$ is an objectwise weak homotopy equivalence. No projective cofibrancy of $D$ is assumed.

source.place: Proposition A.3.3.8(1), printed p.871, together with the Quillen-equivalence criterion.

proof.text: For $T_S\dashv U_S$, apply the Quillen-equivalence criterion in [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation] to $X^{\mathrm{op}}$ and $F=u^*D^{\mathrm{op}}$. Its hypotheses hold: all slice objects are cofibrant and step 4 gives fibrancy of $F$. Since $T_S(X^{\mathrm{op}})=P$ and $f:P\to F$ is weak by step 5, its adjoint $g:X^{\mathrm{op}}\to U_SF$ is a contravariant weak equivalence. It is specifically $g=U_S(f)\circ\eta^T_{X^{\mathrm{op}}}$, and its target is a right fibration. The covariant clause of the same node defines the covariant weak equivalences by simplicial opposite and defines $U_B^{\mathrm{cov}}F=(U_SF)^{\mathrm{op}}$ after the identification $A\cong\mathfrak C[B]$. Thus $g^{\mathrm{op}}:X\to U_B^{\mathrm{cov}}(u^*D^{\mathrm{op}})$ is the required covariant weak equivalence. Its target is a left fibration. This inference uses the ordinary equivalence on opposite slices specified by the cited node.

source.place: Theorem 2.2.1.2 and Remark 2.1.4.12, printed pp.74 and 71; ordinary opposite-base dual.

proof.text: The naturality claimed concerns compatible maps of the input data, including $w$. Write $P_X=T_S(X^{\mathrm{op}})$ and $F_D=u^*D^{\mathrm{op}}$. For $k:X\to X'$ over $B$ and a strict transformation $a:D\to D'$, suppose $w'\,u_!P(k)=a^{\mathrm{op}}w$. Naturality of the Kan-extension adjunction unit gives $f'P(k)=u^*(a^{\mathrm{op}})f$. Naturality of the cone adjunction unit then gives $g'k^{\mathrm{op}}=U_S(u^*(a^{\mathrm{op}}))g$. These are equalities of actual maps, obtained by substituting the two unit formulas in steps 5 and 6. Taking simplicial opposites gives the corresponding covariant square. The adjunctions used are those stated in [lem-coef-unmarked-straightening-target-change] and [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation]. Moreover $\beta_{X'}u_!P(k)=H_C(k)\beta_X$ by the naturality assertion of the target-change node, so the same squares hold when $w$ is presented on $H_C(X)$. Identity maps and composites satisfy these equations by substitution. In particular maps of strict Kan diagrams need not themselves be weak equivalences to give these naturality squares.

source.place: Proposition 2.2.1.1(2), printed p.74, and naturality of the two specified adjunctions.

lean.statement: theorem unmarked_cone_model_comparison (C : Cat.{u, u}) : ∃ K : Data C, Bergner.dwyerKanEquivalences K.u ∧ (∀ (X : Over (nerve C)) (Z : Diagram (Index C)) (i : Z ⟶ (cone K).obj X), IsInitial Z → projectiveCof (Index C) i) ∧ (∀ (X : Over (nerve C)) (D : C ⥤ SSet.{u}), (∀ c : C, KanComplex (D.obj c)) → ∀ w : K.change.kan.obj ((cone K).obj X) ⟶ K.strictOp.obj D, projectiveWeak (discreteCategory C) w → projectiveWeak (Index C) (firstAdjunct K X D w) ∧ contravariantWeak (nerve C).op (secondAdjunct K X D w) ∧ contravariantWeak (nerve C).op ((Over.post opFunctor).map (covariantAdjunct K X D w)) ∧ Enhanced.rightFibration ((K.presentation.U (Index C) K.identityTarget).obj ((targetRestriction K.u).obj (K.strictOp.obj D))).hom ∧ Enhanced.leftFibration ((covariant K).obj ((targetRestriction K.u).obj (K.strictOp.obj D))).hom) ∧ (∀ (X Y : Over (nerve C)) (D E : C ⥤ SSet.{u}) (k : X ⟶ Y) (a : D ⟶ E) (w : K.change.kan.obj ((cone K).obj X) ⟶ K.strictOp.obj D) (w' : K.change.kan.obj ((cone K).obj Y) ⟶ K.strictOp.obj E), (∀ c : C, KanComplex (D.obj c)) → (∀ c : C, KanComplex (E.obj c)) → K.change.kan.map ((cone K).map k) ≫ w' = w ≫ K.strictOp.map a → (cone K).map k ≫ firstAdjunct K Y E w' = firstAdjunct K X D w ≫ (targetRestriction K.u).map (K.strictOp.map a) ∧ (Over.post opFunctor).map k ≫ secondAdjunct K Y E w' = secondAdjunct K X D w ≫ (K.presentation.U (Index C) K.identityTarget).map ((targetRestriction K.u).map (K.strictOp.map a)) ∧ k ≫ covariantAdjunct K Y E w' = covariantAdjunct K X D w ≫ (covariant K).map ((targetRestriction K.u).map (K.strictOp.map a)))
